C01.name: Dead Bug
C01.how: On your back, arms up and hips/knees at 90. Press the lower back into the floor, then lower the opposite arm and leg slowly while keeping it pressed. Exhale on the way down.
C01.caution: The moment the lower back lifts off the floor, you have gone too far.

C02.name: Bird Dog
C02.how: Quadruped, extend opposite arm and leg to a straight line. Hold 5-8s. Keep the hips level - put a light object on the lower back to check.

C03.name: Side Plank
C03.how: Forearm and knees (or feet) supported, body in a straight line, hips stacked and pushed forward. Brace as if about to be punched.
C03.caution: Progress from knees to feet before adding time.

C04.name: McGill Curl-Up
C04.how: One knee bent, one straight. Hands under the lower back to preserve its arch. Lift only the head and shoulders an inch off the floor. Do not flatten the back.
C04.caution: Designed specifically for backs that do not tolerate crunches.

C05.name: Pallof Press
C05.how: Stand side-on to a cable or band at chest height. Press the handle straight out and resist the rotational pull. Ribs down.

C06.name: Copenhagen Plank
C06.how: Side plank with the top leg on a bench, bottom leg hanging. Lift the bottom leg to meet the bench. Start with the knee on the bench, not the ankle.
C06.caution: Very effective but very easy to overdo. Add 5s per week.

C07.name: Suitcase Carry
C07.how: Heavy dumbbell or kettlebell in one hand only. Walk tall, shoulders level, no lean. Switch sides.

M01.name: 90/90 Hip Switch
M01.targets: Hip internal + external rotation, deep rotators
M01.how: Sit with both knees bent 90 deg, one leg in front and one to the side. Keep chest tall, rotate both knees over to the other side without using hands. Pause 2s at the end range each side.
M01.caution: Move slow. If you feel a pinch at the front of the hip, sit on a cushion to raise the hips.

M02.name: Couch Stretch
M02.targets: Rectus femoris, psoas, anterior hip capsule
M02.how: Back foot up on a bench or against a wall, front foot flat. Squeeze the glute of the back leg and tuck the tailbone under before leaning up. The tuck is what makes it work.
M02.caution: Tuck the pelvis first. Arching the lower back to get deeper is exactly what you are trying to fix.

M03.name: Half-Kneeling Hip Flexor w/ Overhead Reach
M03.how: Half-kneeling, tuck the tailbone, squeeze the down-side glute. Reach the same-side arm overhead and side-bend away. Exhale fully at the end range.

M04.name: Cossack Squat
M04.how: Wide stance, shift all weight to one side and sit deep, other leg straight with toes up. Hold a light plate at the chest as a counterweight to stay upright.
M04.caution: Keep the heel of the working leg down. Go only as deep as you can without the lower back rounding.

M05.name: ATG Split Squat
M05.targets: Hip flexor, VMO, knee flexion tolerance
M05.how: Long split stance, drop the back knee toward the floor and let the front knee travel forward over the toes. Chest stays up, back heel lifts.
M05.caution: Bodyweight only for the first 4 weeks.

M07.name: Deep Squat Hold (counterweighted)
M07.targets: Hip, knee, ankle flexion; spinal decompression
M07.how: Hold a 10-15 lb plate at arms length in front, sit into the deepest squat you can with heels down. Use the counterweight to stay upright and relaxed. Breathe.

M08.name: 90/90 Hip Lift with Breathing
M08.targets: Posterior pelvic tilt, deep core, lumbar reset
M08.how: Lie on your back, feet flat on a wall or bench with hips and knees at 90 deg. Exhale hard to tilt the pelvis back and flatten the lower back into the floor, then inhale through the nose without losing the tilt.
M08.caution: This is the single best reset for the anterior-tilt pattern that is loading your lower back.

M09.name: Open Book T-Spine Rotation
M09.how: Side-lying, knees stacked on a foam roller, arms out front. Open the top arm and rotate the chest toward the ceiling, keeping the knees pinned down.
M09.caution: Rotation should come from the ribcage, not the lower back.

M10.name: Cat-Cow
M10.how: Quadruped. Move one vertebra at a time from full flexion to full extension, timed to the breath.

M11.name: Ankle Dorsiflexion Wall Drill
M11.targets: Ankle dorsiflexion (directly limits jump depth and running stride)
M11.how: Toes 4-5 inches from a wall, drive the knee forward over the little toe until it touches the wall without the heel lifting. Back the foot up until it is hard.
M11.caution: Test both sides; the tighter ankle usually matches the tighter hip.

M12.name: Banded Lateral Hip Distraction
M12.how: Heavy band high around the crease of the hip, step away to create tension, then move into a lunge or rock back on all fours. The band pulls the femur away from the socket.

M13.name: Supine Figure-4 Stretch
M13.how: On your back, ankle across the opposite knee, pull the bottom thigh toward you. Keep the head and shoulders down.
M13.caution: Gentle only. Cranking on the piriformis can irritate the sciatic nerve running under it.

M14.name: Sciatic Nerve Glide (supine)
M14.how: On your back, hip at 90 deg, hold behind the thigh. Straighten the knee while pulling the toes toward you, then bend the knee while pointing the toes. Slow, rhythmic, like flossing.
M14.caution: This should NOT reproduce the tingling. Work in the range just short of any symptom. Never stretch into it.

M16.name: Adductor Rock Back
M16.how: Quadruped, one leg extended straight out to the side with the foot flat. Rock the hips back toward the heel.

M17.name: Foam Roll Circuit
M17.how: 60-90s per area: quads, glute/TFL, lats, calves. Then lie back over the roller across the mid-back and extend over it for 10 slow breaths.
M17.caution: Skip direct rolling on the lower back itself; roll the hips and t-spine instead.

M18.name: Bretzel Stretch
M18.targets: Quad, hip flexor, t-spine rotation combined
M18.how: Side-lying, bottom leg bent back and held by the top hand, top leg bent forward and pinned by the bottom hand. Rotate the shoulders back toward the floor and breathe.

M19.name: Standing Hip CARs
M19.targets: Full hip joint control through range
M19.how: Stand tall holding support. Lift one knee to the chest, circle it out to the side, rotate back and extend behind you, then return. Slow and deliberate, 10s per rep.

M20.name: Walk / Easy Spin (active recovery)
M20.how: Easy walk outdoors or 15 min very light bike. Nothing that raises breathing much.
M20.caution: Walking is one of the better things you can do for nerve-related back symptoms.

P01.name: Pogo Hops
P01.targets: Ankle stiffness, achilles elasticity, reactive strength
P01.how: Stiff legs, minimal knee bend, bounce off the balls of the feet. Aim for minimum ground contact time, not maximum height. Think of the ankles as springs.
P01.caution: The single highest-return low-risk jump drill. Quiet landings.

P02.name: Line Hops / Ankling
P02.how: Hop forward and back or side to side over a line as fast as possible, staying on the balls of the feet.

P03.name: A-Skip
P03.targets: Running mechanics, hip flexion, ground stiffness
P03.how: Skip driving one knee to hip height with a dorsiflexed foot, then strike down and back under the hip. Tall posture, arms driving.

P04.name: Snap-Down (Drop and Stick)
P04.how: Stand tall on the toes, then snap down fast into a quarter-squat athletic position and freeze. You are training how to absorb force, which comes before producing it.
P04.caution: Stick every rep dead still for 2s. This is the prerequisite for all box and depth work.

P05.name: Box Jump (step down)
P05.targets: Concentric hip/knee extension power, triple extension
P05.how: Load into a quarter squat, swing the arms, jump onto the box and land softly in the same quarter-squat shape. Step down, never jump down.
P05.caution: Box height should let you land in the same position you took off from. Tucking the knees to your chest to clear a taller box is ego, not training.

P07.name: Squat Jump (non-countermovement)
P07.targets: Pure concentric power, rate of force development
P07.how: Sink to a quarter squat, hold for a full 3s to kill the stretch reflex, then jump as high as possible. No bounce.
P07.caution: Exposes concentric weakness that the bounce hides.

P08.name: Broad Jump
P08.how: Two feet, swing arms back, jump as far forward as possible, land soft in a squat and stick it.
P08.caution: Stick each landing. Do not do these for continuous reps early on.

P10.name: Hurdle Hop (continuous)
P10.how: Line up 4-6 low hurdles or boxes. Hop over each with both feet, minimizing ground contact time between them.
P10.caution: Start at 6-8 inches. Height matters far less than contact time.

P11.name: Alternating Bound
P11.targets: Single-leg power, horizontal force, stride power
P11.how: Exaggerated running leaps, driving the knee up and covering as much ground per stride as possible. Arms drive opposite.

P12.name: Single-Leg Hop (linear)
P12.how: Continuous hops forward on one leg, staying tall and reactive off the ball of the foot.
P12.caution: Do these before you ever attempt one-foot approach jumps at height.

P13.name: Lateral Bound (Skater)
P13.targets: Frontal plane power, glute med, hip stability
P13.how: Push off one leg laterally, land on the other, stick for 1s, then bound back. Land with the knee tracking over the foot.

P14.name: Depth Drop (landing only)
P14.how: Step off a 12-18 inch box, land on both feet in an athletic quarter-squat and freeze. No jump.
P14.caution: The mandatory precursor to depth jumps. Two weeks of these before adding the rebound.

P15.name: Depth Jump
P15.targets: Reactive strength, stretch-shortening cycle, max power
P15.how: Step off a 12-18 inch box, and the instant you touch the ground jump as high as possible. Ground contact should be under 0.25s - it should sound like one bounce, not a thud and a push.
P15.caution: Advanced. Only after depth drops are clean. Full 2 min rest between sets. Never on tired legs.

P17.name: One-Foot Approach Jump
P17.how: 3-4 step approach. The second-to-last step is long and low (the penultimate step), the last is quick - convert horizontal speed into vertical. Reach with the inside hand.
P17.caution: Most people jump 3-5 inches higher off one foot with an approach. This is your fastest route to the rim.

P18.name: Two-Foot Approach Jump
P18.targets: Max vertical off two feet, power step
P18.how: 2-3 step approach into a hop that lands both feet simultaneously, then immediate explosive jump. Arms swing back on the gather and up hard on takeoff.

P20.name: Med Ball Slam
P20.targets: Total body power, lat and core expression
P20.how: Reach the ball overhead with full extension, then slam it down as hard as possible, following through into a hinge.
P20.caution: Hinge at the hips, do not round the lower back to reach the floor.

P21.name: Med Ball Overhead Backward Throw
P21.how: Hold the ball low between the legs, then explosively extend hips, knees and ankles and throw it back over your head as far as possible.
P21.caution: One of the purest measures of triple extension. Throw for distance.

P23.name: Vertical Jump Test
P23.how: Measure standing reach against a wall with chalk. Then take 3 max countermovement jumps and 3 max one-foot approach jumps, marking the highest touch. Record the difference.
P23.caution: Test fresh, at the start of a session, never at the end.

R01.name: Easy Run
R01.targets: Aerobic base, capillary density, fat oxidation
R01.how: Conversational the entire time. If you cannot speak a full sentence, slow down. Target 6:00-6:30 /km.
R01.caution: Roughly 80% of your weekly running should live here. Running easy days too hard is the most common reason people plateau.

R02.name: Long Run
R02.targets: Aerobic endurance, connective tissue, fuel efficiency
R02.how: Steady and comfortable, 5:50-6:20 /km. Last 10 minutes may drift faster if it feels natural.
R02.caution: Build no more than about 1.5 km per week.

R03.name: Tempo / Threshold Run
R03.how: Continuous effort at 4:55-5:05 /km. Comfortably hard - you could speak 3-4 words, not a sentence. 10 min easy either side.
R03.caution: The highest-return single session for a 10k.

R04.name: 1000m Cruise Intervals
R04.how: 1000m reps at 4:50-5:00 /km with 90s easy jog between. Even splits - the last rep should match the first.

R05.name: 400m Repeats
R05.how: 400m at 1:46-1:52 with 90s standing/walking rest. Relaxed face and shoulders, fast legs.
R05.caution: Your old peak set was 9x400. That is the benchmark to chase back.

R06.name: 800m Repeats @ Race Pace
R06.how: 800m at goal 10k pace (3:46 per 800 for a 47:00 finish) with 2 min jog recovery. Learn what the pace feels like.

R07.name: Strides
R07.how: 100m accelerations building to about 90% over the first 40m, hold relaxed, then decelerate. Full walk-back recovery.
R07.caution: Not a sprint. These stay fresh and sharp - add them after easy runs.

R09.name: Fartlek
R09.how: Within an easy run, alternate 1 min hard / 2 min easy. Unstructured effort by feel, not by watch.

R11.name: Recovery Jog / Shakeout
R11.how: Very easy, 6:30+ /km. Short. The goal is to feel better afterward than before.

R12.name: Run Drills (warm-up)
R12.how: A-skips, B-skips, high knees, butt kicks, carioca, leg swings - 20m each.
R12.caution: Do these before every quality session.

R13.name: 10K RACE
R13.how: Warm up 15 min easy plus drills and 3 strides. Go out at goal pace for the first 2 km even if it feels slow. Settle. Work from 5k. Empty the tank from 8k.
R13.caution: The first kilometre run 15s too fast costs you a minute later.

S01.name: Trap Bar Deadlift
S01.targets: Glutes, quads, hamstrings, total posterior chain
S01.how: High handles to start. Hips slightly higher than a squat, chest up, push the floor away. The trap bar keeps the load in line with your body instead of in front of it.
S01.caution: Far kinder to the lower back than a conventional pull. This is your main hinge for the whole block.

S02.name: Trap Bar Jump
S02.targets: Rate of force development, triple extension under load
S02.how: Light load (20-30% of your trap bar 1RM). Dip and jump, leaving the ground a few inches. Reset each rep.
S02.caution: Speed is the point. If the bar is slow, it is too heavy.

S04.name: Front Squat / Safety-Bar Squat
S04.targets: Quads, upper back, trunk - lower spinal shear than back squat
S04.how: Elbows high, bar resting on the front delts (or safety bar handles forward). Upright torso, sit straight down.
S04.caution: The more upright torso puts less extension demand on the lower back. Preferred while symptoms are present.

S05.name: Goblet Squat
S05.how: Dumbbell or kettlebell held at the chest, elbows inside the knees at the bottom. Sit straight down between the heels.

S06.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
S06.targets: Quads, glutes, hip stability, single-leg strength
S06.how: Rear foot on a bench, front foot far enough forward that the shin stays near vertical. Drop straight down, drive through the whole front foot.
S06.caution: The highest-value lower body exercise for jumping that is not a jump. Also spares the spine.

S07.name: High Box Step-Up
S07.targets: Glutes, quads, single-leg drive, hip extension power
S07.how: Box at or just above knee height. Place the whole foot on the box, drive up through the heel without pushing off the back foot. Lower under control.
S07.caution: Resist bouncing off the trailing leg - that is where the exercise gets cheated.

S08.name: Barbell Hip Thrust
S08.targets: Glute max at end range hip extension
S08.how: Shoulder blades on a bench, bar across the hips on a pad, feet flat and shins vertical at the top. Drive the hips up, tuck the ribs down, squeeze hard for 1s.
S08.caution: Do not hyperextend the lower back at the top - the range should come from the hips.

S09.name: Romanian Deadlift
S09.how: Soft knees, push the hips straight back, bar stays in contact with the legs. Stop when the hamstrings reach tension or the back starts to round, whichever is first.
S09.caution: Start light given the nerve symptoms - loaded hamstring tension can provoke them. Build slowly.

S11.name: Nordic Hamstring Curl (eccentric)
S11.how: Kneel with ankles anchored. Lower as slowly as possible under control, catch with the hands, push back up.
S11.caution: The best known hamstring injury preventer. Brutally hard - start with a 3s lower and band assistance.

S12.name: Hamstring Slider Curl
S12.how: Bridge position with heels on sliders or a towel. Extend the legs out keeping the hips up, then pull the heels back in.

S13.name: 45-Degree Back Extension
S13.targets: Glutes and hamstrings, spinal erector endurance
S13.how: Pad just below the hip crease. Round slightly or stay neutral, hinge down and drive up with the glutes, stopping at a straight line.
S13.caution: Stop at straight. Do not arch past neutral at the top.

S16.name: Sled Push
S16.targets: Glutes, quads, calves, horizontal force production, conditioning
S16.how: Low arms, body at a forward angle, drive with short powerful steps and full hip extension. Heavy = strength, light = speed.
S16.caution: Zero spinal compression and zero eccentric load. As close to a free lunch as training offers for a cranky back.

S17.name: Backward Sled Drag
S17.how: Strap or handles, walk backward leaning slightly back, taking short steps and extending the knee fully each step.
S17.caution: Excellent for knee resilience once you start loading jumps.

S19.name: Standing Calf Raise
S19.how: Full range - all the way down for a stretch, all the way up onto the big toe. Pause 1s at the top.
S19.caution: Calves are the last link in the jump chain and the most commonly under-trained.

S20.name: Seated Calf Raise
S20.targets: Soleus (the muscle that matters most for running)
S20.how: Knees bent at 90, full range, slow 2s lower and 1s pause at the top.
S20.caution: The soleus takes more load per stride than any other muscle while running.

S21.name: Tibialis Raise
S21.targets: Tibialis anterior, shin splint resistance, ankle balance
S21.how: Heels against a wall, lean back, lift the toes toward the shins as high as possible and lower slowly.
S21.caution: Cheap insurance as running volume climbs.

S22.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
S22.how: One leg, off a step for full range, hold a support for balance only.
S22.caution: Aim to work toward 20+ clean reps per side.

U01.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
U01.how: Feet planted, slight arch, lower to the chest under control, press without letting the elbows flare to 90.

U03.name: Overhead Press
U03.how: Standing, brace the trunk and squeeze the glutes, press straight overhead and finish with the biceps by the ears.
U03.caution: Ribs down. Leaning back to press is a lower-back cost you do not need.

U04.name: Pull-Up / Lat Pulldown
U04.how: Full hang to chin over the bar. Pull the elbows down and back, do not shrug.

U05.name: Chest-Supported Row
U05.how: Chest on an incline bench, row the dumbbells toward the hips, squeeze the shoulder blades.
U05.caution: Chest support takes the lower back entirely out of it.

U07.name: Face Pull
U07.how: Rope at face height, pull toward the forehead with the elbows high, finish with the hands wide.
U07.caution: Direct antidote to the desk posture.

U08.name: Push-Up
U08.how: Rigid plank from heels to head, elbows about 45 degrees to the body.

X06.name: Sled Push-Pull Circuit
X06.targets: Full body conditioning with no eccentric damage
X06.how: Push 20m, turn and drag backward 20m. That is one round. Rest 60-90s.
X06.caution: The best conditioning option on the list for someone protecting their lower back.
